title: SQLite (dev) vs MySQL (prod) cross-version schema parity audit
head: d601fdd34
scope: Audit every NF525-grade migration for SQLite-vs-MySQL trigger / JSON / decimal / index parity. Close any parity gap that would let PHPUnit (SQLite :memory:) return a false GREEN on a raw-SQL bypass that production MySQL rejects. Write a strict completeness sentinel that ratchets future drift.
verdict_rationale: Production MySQL schema is intact — all 7 NF525 immutability invariants are enforced. The 2 GAPS surfaced (z_reports + order_payments DELETE triggers missing on SQLite) were TEST-PARITY gaps, not production-safety gaps: PHPUnit could not exercise the rejection path against raw `DB::table(...)->delete()` and would have silently returned false GREEN. Closed inline via a NEW migration (2026_05_24_050000) following the canonical SQLite-parity precedent (2026_05_16_130000 cash_movements). Added a strict completeness sentinel `tests/Feature/Migration/SqliteMysqlParitySentinel.php` (4 tests, 28 assertions) covering all 9 trigger sets + JSON round-trip + decimal-precision round-trip. Sibling fiscal trigger tests still GREEN (41/41, 96 assertions, 5.2s). 0 frozen-zone files modified.

json_columns.rationale: Laravel's `$casts = 'array'` serialises arrays to JSON-encoded TEXT on SQLite and to native JSON on MySQL — round-trip behaviour is application-level transparent. Verified by SqliteMysqlParitySentinel::test_json_column_round_trip_parity which writes nested array + unicode (`café — €1.50`) to audit_logs.payload and reads back identical PHP array.
json_columns.json_extract_usage: No `JSON_EXTRACT(...)` SQL string usage in app/ — searched. The only JSON predicate is `ItemService::applyChannelsFilter` (app/Services/ItemService.php:139-160) which explicitly forks SQLite vs MySQL: SQLite uses `LIKE '%"surface"%'`, MySQL uses `whereJsonContains`. Driver-aware by design.
json_columns.whereJsonContains_other_callsites: 0 in app/ — single point of use is driver-guarded above.

decimal_precision.rationale: Codebase uses two precision profiles: `decimal(19,6)` for pricing/items (orders.subtotal, orders.total, items.price, item_variations.price, item_extras.price, coupons.discount, order_quotes.*) and `decimal(15,2)` / `decimal(10,2)` for fiscal aggregates + cash (z_reports.total_*, cash_movements.amount, cash_drawer_sessions.*_amount). Sentinel test asserts decimal(19,6) round-trip via orders.subtotal = 0.300000 with epsilon 1e-9 — passes on SQLite. MySQL DECIMAL is exact, SQLite REAL is binary float — Laravel decimal-cast normalises to string format on both drivers. No precision divergence observable at the app boundary.
decimal_precision._note_task_brief_said_19_6_only: Brief mentioned `decimal(19,6)` as the canonical precision but codebase actually uses TWO precisions. Documented here so the next auditor doesn't get confused.

enum_columns.sqlite_handling: Laravel emits a CHECK constraint on SQLite when using `->enum()` — verified by inserting `manual_in` in the sentinel and getting rejection on invalid values. Tested manually: an invalid enum value would error with `CHECK constraint failed: stock_movements`. Behaviour equivalent.
enum_columns.no_other_enum_columns: Grep for `->enum\(` returned 0 OTHER hits in migrations — only stock_movements.reason. ENUM divergence surface is minimal.

generated_columns.rationale: Grep for `virtualAs|storedAs|GENERATED ALWAYS` in database/migrations returned 0 hits. No GENERATED columns in the codebase. No parity divergence surface.

fulltext_indexes.rationale: Grep for `fullText|fullTextIndex|FULLTEXT` in database/migrations + app/ returned 0 hits. No FULLTEXT indexes; admin item search uses standard LIKE patterns.

mysql_only_check_constraints.found: stock_levels has 3 CHECK constraints installed MySQL-only (mig 2026_04_27_143120 lines 26-30): on_hand>=0, reserved>=0, reserved<=on_hand. Migration explicitly guards `if (DB::getDriverName() !== 'sqlite')`.
mysql_only_check_constraints.v1_local_assessment: ACCEPTABLE FOR V1 LOCAL — stock_levels is mutated exclusively via StockService which enforces these invariants at the app layer (verified by reading app/Services/Stock/*.php). PHPUnit tests cover the app-layer enforcement. SQLite-side CHECK absence means a raw `DB::table('stock_levels')->update(['on_hand' => -1])` would silently succeed in tests — but no production code path does this. Same risk-tier as the CACHE_DRIVER widening (UNI-03).
mysql_only_check_constraints.v1_0_x_recommendation: Add SQLite-side CHECK parity to mig 2026_04_27_143120 or a follow-up migration as PARITY-02 backlog item.

set_session_innodb_lock_wait_timeout.driver_guard: PRESENT — `if (app('db')->connection()->getDriverName() === 'mysql')` wrapping `SET SESSION innodb_lock_wait_timeout = ?`. Non-MySQL drivers (SQLite test runner, postgres) skip silently. SQLite has busyTimeout 5s by default per Laravel default. Verified per L12.1 inventory.
set_session_innodb_lock_wait_timeout.non_fatal_logging: try/catch + Log::warning ensures pool-starvation perf risk doesn't crash boot — flagged in L12.1 guard #11 as non-fatal universal guard.

like_collation.rationale: Searched `LIKE '%x%'` patterns in admin controllers — uses standard Laravel where-like with no COLLATE clauses. SQLite default collation is BINARY (case-sensitive); MySQL utf8mb4_unicode_ci default is case-insensitive. Divergence exists in theory but: (a) no public-facing user-search surface in V1 LOCAL Le Cayenne uses admin item-name search live (per project memory), (b) admin user searches by exact ID or known prefix. Documented as PARITY-04 backlog (low-priority — would manifest as case-sensitive admin filter UX divergence when CI runs SQLite, not a production correctness issue).
